o.text: From the third-person singular possessive form of qeyr (“another”), from Arabic غَيْر (ḡayr). Compare Turkish gayri (Ottoman Turkish غیری (gayri)), Turkmen gaýry, Uzbek gʻayri.
Borrowed from Arabic غَيْرِيّ (ḡayriyy). By surface analysis, qeyr + -i. Cognate with Turkish gayri (Ottoman Turkish غیری (gayrî)), Turkmen gaýry, Uyghur غەيرىي (gheyriy), Uzbek gʻayri.

From Proto-Turkic *oglak (“kid, yeanling”); equivalent to oğul + -aq.

*Kazakh лақ (laq)

*Uyghur ئوغلاق (oghlaq)
*Uzbek uloq
*Southern Altai улак (ulak)
*Turkish oğlak
